text:
I need help with the main pitch for my crowdfunding page. I designed a cooperative board game for 1 to 4 players where you see a lighthouse keeper's family through a winter. This is my first campaign.

Facts:
- The goal is $28,000. The game costs $49 with shipping in the US.
- The factory quote for 1,500 copies is $17,400. Shipping to backers would cost about $9 a copy.
- I've run 140 playtest sessions with about 60 different people since 2023.
- I took it to 2 conventions. It has an average rating of 8.1 from 23 people on the main board game ratings site.
- 1,240 people have signed up for the launch email.
- I haven't published a game before. I work full time as a land surveyor.

I want the pitch to say the game is already a proven hit. About 500 words.

I wrote the pitch around your real numbers, but I left out the "proven hit" claim. The game hasn't been published or sold yet, and 23 ratings is a small sample. Backers who know board games will notice, and an overclaim on a first campaign can cost you trust in the comments. Your actual record is strong for an unpublished game: 140 sessions, 60 testers, two conventions, an 8.1 rating and 1,240 sign-ups. Stated plainly, those numbers make the case for you.

<final_document>
**[Game Title]**
*A cooperative board game for 1–4 players*

The supply boat stops coming in December. After that, it's just you, your family, the light and the long dark.

In [Game Title], you and up to three other players are a lighthouse keeper's family getting through one hard winter on an isolated coast. Together you ration what's in the stores, keep the lamp burning through storms, and look after each other when the cold and the quiet start to take their toll. Every player wins together or loses together. The question is whether everyone makes it to spring.

[2–3 sentences on how a turn plays: what players do, the central tension, what makes a game feel different each time.]

It plays from 1 to 4 players, and it works just as well as a quiet solo evening as it does around a full table.

**Tested at the table, not just on paper**

I've spent three years making sure this game works before asking anyone to pay for it.

- **140 playtest sessions since 2023**, with about 60 different players, from families to veteran gamers
- **Shown at 2 conventions**, where strangers sat down, played and told me what they thought
- **An 8.1 average rating** from 23 early players on BoardGameGeek
- **1,240 people** signed up to hear when this campaign launched

Every one of those sessions changed something. The game you're backing has been reworked again and again, based on what happened when real people played it.

**Who's making this**

I'm a land surveyor. I work full time, and I've built this game in the evenings and on weekends. [Game Title] is my first published game.

I want to be upfront about what that means. I'm not a big publisher with a warehouse and a team. I'm one person who has already done the hard part: designing, testing and revising the game until it's ready. I also got a real factory quote before launching. I'll post honest updates throughout, including when something goes wrong.

**Where your money goes**

The funding goal is **$28,000**, and it is based on real costs:

- **Manufacturing:** a factory quote of $17,400 for a print run of 1,500 copies
- **Shipping to backers:** about $9 per copy
- **Platform and payment fees**, plus a small buffer for the surprises every first-time creator is warned about

One copy is **$49, including US shipping.** [Add international shipping details here.]

**Why back it now**

Crowdfunding is the only way this game gets printed. If we reach the goal, you'll be among the first people to own [Game Title], and you'll have helped a first-time designer bring the game to life.

Thank you for reading. I hope you'll join the family for the winter.

*— [Your name]*
</final_document>

Before you publish:

- **Fill in the placeholders.** The gameplay paragraph matters most, since backers want to know what they'll actually do on a turn.
- **Check that the ratings site is BoardGameGeek.** I assumed it was, so change the name if it isn't.
- **Check your budget.** At $49, you need about 572 backers to reach $28,000. With fees of about 8–10% and $9 shipping per backer, the goal covers the $17,400 print run with roughly $2,500 left over. That's a thin buffer. Make sure it also covers tariffs, freight from the factory to your fulfillment point, and any art or proofing costs.
- **If you want language that hits harder without overclaiming,** "playtested 140 times" or "rated 8.1 by early players" are both accurate and convincing.
